title: Exposure chronicle and decision protocols (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a chronological journal of exposure decisions for multi-wave canaries and AB slices.
- Make explicit the human decision path: what signals were considered, who signed off, what mitigations were chosen.
- Provide a lightweight, searchable artifact to help post-mortem and to reduce tribal knowledge.

Scope:
- Applies to product console rollouts that: change model routing, introduce new rerankers, change reranking thresholds, or modify safety-filtering heuristics.
- Not for infra-only capacity changes (SRE keeps separate incident timeline).

How to use this doc (quick):
- During active exposure, each steward appends a timestamped entry describing: traffic fraction, observed signals, decision, and next action. Keep entries terse.
- Use the template in "Entry format" below.
- Tag entries with gate name (e.g., "early-telemetry", "human-review", "escalation-1").

Entry format (copy/paste):
- timestamp: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm UTC
- steward: name (role)
- traffic: cohort/route + percent
- signals: bullets of top 3 delta signals seen (latency, error rate, quality/regression metric)
- decision: continue / hold / rollback / widen / narrow + brief rationale
- actions: immediate steps (rollback command, increase sampling, open PR, notify oncall)
- links: links to dashboards / PRs / slack threads

Operational heuristics (recommended):
- Minimum 30 minutes of steady-state at each step before final decision unless severity > critical.
- If error rate increases > 3x baseline for two consecutive 5-min windows, auto-hold and notify SRE.
- Latency P95 increase > 40% and conversions drop > 5% -> human gate required.
- Quality regressions measured via eval-set: delta > 2% BAD -> hold.

Decision gates and roles (who does what):
- Steward (product owner) : owns hypothesis, convenes stakeholders, makes initial call.
- Observability lead (console/telemetry) : summarizes signals, runs quick root-cause checks.
- SRE oncall : evaluates infra signals, approves capacity-based widen/rollback.
- Safety reviewer : assesses behavioral/safety regressions and approves human-review escalations.
- Release coordinator : executes traffic shifts in the Console and records the action.

Canary sizing & slicing guidance:
- Start tiny: first slice = 0.1%-0.5% of traffic for model/behavior changes (use lower bound for high-risk verticals).
- Microcohorts: pick 3 orthogonal slices (new users, power users, region-eu) rather than random to detect context-specific regressions.
- For A/B experiments that affect UX conversion, bias slice composition to representative segments and make sure sample sizes are precomputed.

Observability checklist (dashboards / quick queries):
- Traffic and routing: per-route qps, request types, token distribution.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 + tail-flush counts.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx, model-decoder-errors, streaming disconnects.
- Quality: eval-set pass@k, rerank delta, hallucination proxies (entity-mismatch rate).
- Business: conversion/CTR/retention probes if applicable.
- Cost: token-per-response average (for Dedicated customers this can trigger SLA/billing alarms).

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Tier 1: Steward + Observability lead — immediate assessment, decide continue/hold for 30m.
- Tier 2: Add SRE oncall and Safety reviewer — for sustained infra or safety signals; possible rollback within 15m.
- Tier 3: Exec oncall + Legal/Compliance — for sensitive/regulatory exposures, stop traffic and start incident channel.

Decision examples (realistic snippets):
- 2025-02-18 15:12 UTC | steward: Priya Nambiar (product) | traffic: alpha-route v2 -> 0.3% | signals: p95 latency +22% (db cache miss spike), error 5xx up 0.6% -> decision: hold, narrow to 0.1% while SRE investigates | actions: opened RW-4821, slack #canary-alpha, increased sampling to log body, links: dashboard RW-canary-alpha

- 2025-02-25 09:40 UTC | steward: Marcus Lee (release) | traffic: ab-test B variant -> 10% | signals: quality eval delta -1.6% pass@10, conversion flat -> decision: continue but flag for extended eval on cohort 'new-users' | actions: scheduled 24h follow-up, added safety reviewer in rotation, links: github PR 128

Pre-launch checklist (to attach before first exposure):
- [ ] Hypothesis written and success/fail metrics explicit (include eval-set anchors).
- [ ] Rollback procedure documented and confirmed with release coordinator.
- [ ] Dashboards and alert thresholds created and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Oncall rotation notified and paged test succeeded.
- [ ] Canary steward assigned and comms channel created.

Post-exposure required outputs (within 72h):
- Short chronicle: one-paragraph summary of what happened and why.
- Signal appendix: time-series snippets and anchored metrics.
- Actions log: PRs, config changes, incident tickets.
- Lessons learned / decisions to bake into runbook.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define a single source-of-truth for delta-quality metrics; multiple teams currently compute slightly different baselines. (owner: Observability)
- Should we automate the "hold" action at 3x error rate for all hosted tiers? Tradeoff: false positive interruptions vs faster protection. (owner: SRE + Product)
- Align microcohort definitions across GA experiments to avoid cross-experiment contamination. (owner: Product-ops)

Next steps (short):
- Convert this chronicle template into a Console micro-form that auto-populates timestamps and steward identity (owner: Devex).
- Pilot the chronicle on the next two ramped releases and collect feedback at steward retro.
- Write a short training doc for stewards with examples and roleplay scenarios.

Notes to self / shorthand (messy):
- keep entries short; heavy-lifting goes into post-exposure appendix.
- prefer explicit numbers over adjectives (eg: show p95 from baseline not "slower").
- always include links to the exact dashboard slice used.

If you're actively running a canary now - add an entry below rather than editing historical lines. Chronology is the point.

-- end of working notes --
